Compliance with the Borough's unfit buildings and housing standards ordinances

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Compliance Application for Sale (owner, buyer, rooms, signature) and file it with the Building Department at Borough Hall, 106 Brown Avenue, with payment by cash, check or money order. Call for an inspection appointment. Certificate of Occupancy inspections are held Monday 1:30 to 2:30 pm and Tuesday and Thursday 2:00 to 2:30 pm.

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Compliance is required when a house or business is about to be sold. We inspect for working smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors. Smoke detectors work best one in every bedroom. Carbon monoxide is required one per floor.
Cash, checks or money orders are the accepted payment options.

resale_co.notes: The Housing Department page and the Certificate of Compliance Application for Sale (PDF last modified June 9, 2026) both require a Certificate of Compliance when a house is sold, with the inspection covering smoke and carbon monoxide alarms; fees are $75.00 (1 family), $150.00 (2 family), $225.00 (3 family); the page also lists $100.00 for commercial. No reinspection fee, lead time or validity period is published. The sale form is bundled with a fire safety sheet headed 'Fire Safety Inspection Requirements - For Rental' that lists the smoke, CO and fire extinguisher rules; the page and the sheet differ on CO placement (one per floor vs within 10 feet of bedrooms). Appointments: the Housing Department page says to call 201-249-1189 (the form labels it the Code Enforcement Officer's mobile number), so the office line (973) 790-7902 ext. 524 is given as the main phone. Construction Official James Booth shares ext. 524 (Construction@prospectpark.net). Rental programs are separate: a $50.00 Certificate of Occupancy for every change of tenant, and absentee landlords register yearly for $100.00.

fire_cert.notes: Prospect Park is the only town in this group where the State (NJ DCA) is the fire code enforcing agency (registry code S). The state fire directory (survey 1/12/2026) still names the NJ Division of Fire Safety, (609) 633-6132, under Smoke Detector Compliance. But the DCA list of state-enforced towns (revised 7/17/2026) lists PROSPECT PARK 1610 without the 'SC = Smoke Certs' mark, and the DCA smoke certificate portal data (read 2026-10-02) lists PROSPECT PARK BORO-001 with jurisdiction State and smoke-certificate exempt = true, the same flags used for towns that issue the certificate themselves. The Borough's own Certificate of Compliance for sale explicitly includes the smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm inspection. So the smoke/CO check most likely happens through the Borough's Certificate of Compliance ($75 / $150), and the state portal fees ($45 / $90 / $161) are recorded only as the current DCA source. Confirm with the Borough before relying on either. The Prospect Park Volunteer Fire Department (Chief Douglas Struyk, 973-790-7902 ext. 526) and Fire Safety Director Daniel Cabrera (ext. 522 per the Borough directory) handle emergency response and fire safety, not resale certificates as far as the site shows. The directory email for DCA is blank; DCA's portal page lists BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov only for homes not subject to the CO requirement.
